newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-Alcoa Australia says it plans to cut jobs.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-Alcoa Australia says it plans to cut jobs.

text.p: Alcoa of Australia plans to cut some jobs over the next 12 months as part of a global plan by 60 percent parent Aluminum Co of America to lay off 2,900 workers, a spokesman for Alcoa of Australia said on Monday.
"We will be cutting some personnel, but the level will be lower than in the U.S.," the spokesman said, adding that a final figure on the number of job losses had not yet been determined.
All of the job cuts from the Australian company would come from administrative and head office operations, located in Victoria and New South Wales states, the spokesman said.
Alcoa of Australia employs about 6,000 people.

The U.S. parent announced on Friday that US$60 million of a US$65.5 million after-tax charge against its 1996 third quarter earnings would be used for permanent layoffs and to fund incentives for employees who volunteer to leave.
WMC Ltd holds a 39.25 percent stake in Alcoa of Australia, with the remaining 0.75 percent held by institutions.
